questions.q: In optical communication systems operating at $1200nm$, only $2 %$ of the source frequency is available for TV transmission having a bandwidth of $5MHz$. The number of TV channels that can be transmitted is ${10}^{n}$. The value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
The frequency of optical communication is given by,

$v = \dfrac{c}{\lambda}$ or $v = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{1200 \times {10}^{- 9}}$

$v = 25 \times {10}^{13}Hz$

But only $2 %$ of the source frequency is available for TV transmission.

${v}^{′} = 2 .5 \times {10}^{14} \times 2%$

${v}^{′} = 2 .5 \times {10}^{14} \times \dfrac{2}{100}$

${v}^{′} = 5 \times {10}^{12}Hz$

$∴ Numberofchannels = \dfrac{{v}^{′}}{bandwidth}$

$Noofchannels = \dfrac{{5 \times 10}^{12}}{{5 \times 10}^{6}} = {10}^{6} = 1million$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider telecommunication through optical fibres. Which of the following statements is not true?
options: optical fibres can be of graded refractive index
optical fibres are subjected to electro-magnetic interference from outside
optical fibres have extremely low transmission loss
optical fibres may have homogeneous core with a suitable cladding
questions.solution:
Some of the characteristics of an optical fibre are as follows.

(i) This works on the principle of total internal reflection.

(ii) It consists of core made up of glass/silica/plastic with refractive index ${n}_{1},$ which is surrounded by a glass or plastic cladding with refractive index ${n}_{2}\left({n}_{2} > {n}_{1}\right).$ The refractive index of cladding can be either changing abruptly or gradually changing (Graded index fibre).

(iii) There is a very little transmission loss through optical fibres.

(iv) There is no interference from stray electric and magnetic fields to the signals through optical fibres.

superimposing a low frequency signal on a high frequency carrier signal

questions.q: What is the modulation index of an FM signal having a carrier swing of $100kHz$ when the modulating signal has a frequency of $8kHz$?
questions.solution:
Given: Carrier Swing $= 100kHz$

${f}_{a} = 8kHz$

From the defining equation,

${m}_{f} = \dfrac{∆ f}{{f}_{a}}$

First determining $∆ f$ ,

$∆ f = \dfrac{CarrierSwing}{2}$

$= \dfrac{100 \times {10}^{3}}{2}$

$= 50kHz$

Now substituting into the equation for ${m}_{f}$

${m}_{f} = \dfrac{50 \times {10}^{3}}{8 \times {10}^{3}}$

$= 6.25$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The antenna current of an AM transmitter is $8A$ when only the carrier is sent, but it increases to $8. 93A$ when the carrier is modulated by a single sine wave. Find the percentage modulation.
options:
$60. 1 %$
&
questions.solution:
The power dissipated in any circuit is a function of the square of voltage across the circuit and the effective resistance of the circuit. Equation of AM wave reveals that it has three components of amplitude Clearly; power output must be distributed among these components.

Carrier power, ${P}_{c} = \dfrac{{\left({E}_{c} / \sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}{R} = \dfrac{{E}_c^{2}}{2R}$

Total power of side bands,

${P}_{S} = \dfrac{{\left(m{E}_{c} / 2\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}{R} + \dfrac{{\left(m{E}_{c} / 2\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}{R} = \dfrac{m^{2}{E}_c^{2}}{4R}$

$∴ \dfrac{{P}_{S}}{{P}_{C}} = \dfrac{1}{2}m^{2}$

and ${P}_{T} = {P}_{C} + {P}_{S} = {P}_{C} \left(1 + \dfrac{m^{2}}{2}\right)

$∴ $\dfrac{{P}_{T}}{{P}_{C}} =1 + \dfrac{m^{2}}{2}$⇒ {$\left(\dfrac{{I}_{T}}{{I}_{C}}\right)$}^{2} = 1 + $\dfrac{m^{2}}{2}

Given that, ${I}_{T} = 8.93A, {I}_{C} = 8A, m = ?$

$∴ {$\left(\dfrac{8.93}{8}\right)$}^{2} = 1 + $\dfrac{m^{2}}{2}

Or 1.246 = 1 + \dfrac{m^{2}}{2}$ or$\dfrac{m^{2}}{2} =0.246$

Or $m = \sqrt{2 \times 0.246} =0.701 = 70.1%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The maximum electron density in the ionosphere in the morning is ${10}^{10}m^{- 3}.$ At noon time, it increases to $2 \times {10}^{10}m^{- 3}.$ Find the ratio of critical frequency at noon and the critical frequency in the morning.
questions.solution:
Given, the maximum electron density in the morning

${N}_\max = {10}^{10}m^{- 3}$

${f}_c^{'} = 9{\left({N}_\max\right)}^{1 / 2} = 9{\left({10}^{10}\right)}^{1 / 2}$

Critical frequency ${f}_c^{′} = 9 \times {10}^{5}$

The maximum electron density at noon

${N}_\max = {2 \times 10}^{10}m^{- 3}$

Critical frequency

${f}_c^{′′} = 9 \times \left({N}_\max^{′}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = 9 \times \left(2 \times {10}^{10}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = 9 \times \sqrt{2} \times {10}^{5}$

The ratio of critical frequency at noon and critical frequency in the morning.

$\dfrac{{f}_c^{′′}}{{f}_c^{′}} = \dfrac{9 \times \sqrt{2} \times {10}^{5}}{9 \times {10}^{5}}$

Or $\dfrac{{f}_c^{′′}}{{f}_c^{′}} = \sqrt{2} = 1.414$
